**Data coverage (read this first).** Only one of the three sources returned usable data for AMD for 2026-11-13 to 2026-11-20. Yahoo Finance news returned DATA_UNAVAILABLE (YFDataException). Reddit (r/wallstreetbets, r/stocks, r/investing) failed to fetch. Neither failure says anything about AMD or about whether discussion exists. That leaves a single 12-message StockTwits snapshot, with every message timestamped within about 20 minutes on 2026-11-20 (21:26Z to 21:47Z). It captures one moment, not a week of sentiment, and there is no institutional or news context to check it against.

**1. StockTwits (the only available source)**
- The "Screened by Jev" classifier kept 12 of 30 fetched posts as on-topic for AMD. Its stance read was 6 bullish, 3 bearish, 1 neutral and 2 unclear. That is 6 of 9 directional posts (about 67%) bullish, which on its own is moderately bullish.
- The user-applied tags are much thinner: 2 Bullish (17%), 2 Bearish (17%), 8 unlabeled. That is an even 50/50 split on only 4 tagged posts, so it signals uncertainty and nothing more.
- The classifier's more bullish read comes from untagged posts that it interpreted as bullish. Examples are "AMD is the new king in the market", "way oversold on amd… buy this area is pretty safe", and the price-target calls for 500 and 600. These are plausible bullish readings, but they are inferences, not user labels.
- **Distress and drawdown tone.** Several posts describe losses or a sharp drop. One reads "I am down significantly!" Another is a long-term holder saying "Sorry you longs are going through this, it's rough." Another says "way oversold." This pattern fits a sharp recent selloff.
- **Capex-pullback narrative.** One post says AMD "was down 6.5 percent in premarket, per reports", and that "investors are bracing for a capex pullback, and component makers get priced first when that fear spreads". Another post argues AI valuations had no fundamental basis and are "coming back to reality". The post is retail commentary, and the 6.5% figure is unverified because no news source was available to confirm it.
- **Price-level claims conflict and are unreliable.** Bullish posts call for "Back to 500 next week" and "Monday 600". A bearish post says "$NVDA below $80, $AMD below $150", and another jokes about NVDA at $40. These cannot all describe the same price. Some are probably sarcasm, hyperbole or trolling. I did not treat any of them as reliable price information, and none can be checked against the evidence provided.
- **Bearish posts are low-quality.** One is a political rant about moving companies to China. The other is an "AI bubble / overvaluation" one-liner with the implausible price levels above. Neither gives fundamental evidence.

**2. Cross-source divergence/alignment.** None can be assessed, because news and Reddit are both missing. Within StockTwits there is an internal gap: the classifier leans bullish (about 2:1), while user tags are split evenly and the content shows loss-stricken holders and dip-buying calls together. That pattern often shows up after a sharp drop, when sentiment is contested and dip-buyers are active.

**3. Dominant themes.**
- (a) A sharp one-day drop, with a premarket decline of about 6.5% reported by one user.
- (b) AI-capex-pullback and AI-valuation-bubble worries spreading across semiconductors (NVDA, MU, SMCI are mentioned alongside AMD).
- (c) Dip-buying and "oversold" calls.
- (d) Hype and unverifiable price targets.

**4. Catalysts and risks surfaced by the data.**
- Risk: a continued AI-capex fear trade, with sector-wide de-rating of chip names.
- Risk: retail-holder stress, which can feed further selling if the drop extends.
- Possible upside: oversold bounce attempts and an expected "data rally" that a poster says depends on chips leading.
- No company-specific event (earnings, product launch, guidance) is cited in the provided evidence, and I cannot confirm the cause of the drop.

**5. Overall read.** Retail sentiment is mixed: a modest bullish lean from the classifier and dip-buyers, set against visible losses and macro/AI-capex anxiety. The sample is small, covers one moment, and is noisy, so confidence is low. This is a signal to weigh alongside fundamentals and technicals, not a price call.

# AMD Weekly News and Macro Report (2026-11-13 to 2026-11-20)

## Data coverage and limits
- **Company news (`get_news`)**: the first call (11/13–11/20) failed with a Yahoo Finance error. A second call (11/16–11/20) returned headlines only, with no article bodies. Everything below on AMD comes from those headlines, and I haven't verified the details inside the articles.
- **FRED macro data**: all four pulls (fed funds, 10-year Treasury, CPI, unemployment) failed because the API key isn't configured. I have no actual rate, yield, inflation or jobs figures. The macro view rests on headlines and prediction markets only.
- **Missing data**: I have no AMD price levels, volume, or implied volatility. I also couldn't confirm the dates of some headlines, such as the "down 26%" and "crashed nearly 8%" items.

## 1. The week in one line
A violent, AI-led semiconductor selloff, with AMD at the center, is hitting a market that is also pricing a hawkish Fed.

## 2. Market backdrop
- **Index damage**: Yahoo Finance's live blog for 11/19 says the Dow and S&P 500 entered correction and the Nasdaq sank about 5%, erasing its 2026 gains. It describes the AI trade as "melting down."
- **Friday 11/20**: Motley Fool's midday note says the Nasdaq plunged nearly 3%, with "AMD and Micron lead[ing] a brutal semiconductor sell-off." The selloff was still running at the time of the latest data.
- **Nvidia**: headlines report a 12% drop in a single session and "down 37% in a month." Even a bullish TipRanks piece on Nvidia's demand visibility into 2029 shows the debate has turned to valuation and risk, not demand. Trefis is also questioning Nvidia's $81B receivables pile.
- **Sector spillover**:
  - Broadcom fell on a Barron's-reported claim that Google is cutting AI chip shipments.
  - TSMC fell 4.76% as Taiwan logged its worst week since 1991.
  - Sandisk shares sank on the first day of an 8-for-1 split.
- **Catalyst**: Anthropic's Nasdaq debut. Its stock reportedly dropped 8% after a strong IPO pop. Barron's explicitly ties AMD's drop to "Anthropic's drop and a short report." Anthropic is a large AI compute buyer, so its post-IPO weakness feeds directly into AI-capex sentiment.

## 3. AMD-specific news (headline level)
1. **Selloff**: Zacks reports AMD "crashed nearly 8%" in one session. Yahoo says AMD and Broadcom "extend declines." Motley Fool puts AMD down 26% (period unclear) against Intel down 42%.
2. **Short report**: Barron's mentions a short report weighing on the stock alongside the Anthropic move. I couldn't see its author or claims.
3. **China export headline**: TipRanks, citing Hunterbrook, says congressional files detail AMD's requests to export AI chips to China. This is a policy and regulatory overhang, and a possible reputational one. I don't know the contents or whether licenses were granted.
4. **Relative framing**: media comparisons now pit AMD against Intel as "buy the dip" candidates. That signals dip-buying interest but not a confirmed bottom.

## 4. Macro and policy read (prediction markets)
- **December FOMC (resolves 12/9)**:
  - 25bp hike: 90%, up 1.0pp on the week.
  - No change: 9%, up 6.2pp.
  - 50bp+ hike: 2%, down 5.8pp.
  - Any cut: about 0%.
- **Full-year cuts**: "No Fed cuts in 2026" is 98%.
- **Reading this**: the market is pricing a hike, not easing, and an MT Newswires headline cites a "hawkish Fed." That is a hostile setup for long-duration growth and semiconductor stocks. I couldn't verify the current policy rate or inflation data. Treat the 90% hike figure as a market-implied probability to check against FOMC communications, not as confirmed fact.
- **Recession**: US recession by end of 2026 is 4% (up 2.1pp). Japan is 14% (up 4.5pp) and the UK is 2%, both on thin volume. The market sees this as a sentiment and valuation shock, not a growth collapse.
- **AI bubble**: "AI bubble burst in 2026?" is 62%, up 54.7pp in a week, on $3.3M volume. This is the clearest quantified read on sentiment: the market moved from largely dismissing a bubble to treating it as likely within days.
- **Other markets**: "Nvidia largest company by market cap on 12/31" is 4% (down 4.5pp). Anthropic reaching a $3T valuation is 3%. No Polymarket markets exist for Taiwan or China semiconductor risk, so geopolitical risk can't be quantified there. The Taiwan market stress is visible only in the TSMC and Taiwan headlines.

## 5. Trading implications
- **Regime**: this looks like a de-risking and deleveraging move across AI hardware, not an AMD-specific event. Correlation across NVDA, AVGO, MU, TSM and AMD is high, so single-name views are secondary to the sector tape.
- **Downside risks**:
  - The Fed hikes in December.
  - More reports of AI chip order cuts, as in the Google/Broadcom item.
  - The AMD short report and the China export story develop further.
  - Anthropic and other recent AI IPOs keep falling, which could feed back into AI capex expectations.
  - Taiwan stress escalates.
- **Upside or stabilization signals to watch**:
  - Stabilization in NVDA and TSM.
  - A softer tone from the Fed.
  - Substantive rebuttals of the short report.
  - The AI-bubble probability stopping its climb.
- **Positioning**: with the Nasdaq down about 5% in a session and falling again the next day, volatility is likely extreme. Risk-management points:
  - Size down, and use defined-risk structures. Options pricing is likely elevated, but I have no implied-volatility data.
  - Don't catch the falling knife without confirmation, such as a stabilizing sector tape.
  - Avoid weekend gap risk if you're leveraged.
- **Dated events to watch**: FOMC on 12/9 and any Fed speakers before it, the CPI and jobs releases once data access is restored, and follow-up on the short report and export-license reporting.

## 6. Summary table

| Taiwan | Worst week since 1991 | GuruFocus | Medium | Supply-chain and geopolitical tail risk, not quantifiable in prediction markets |
| Fed (Dec 9) | 90% 25bp hike, 9% hold, about 0% cut; 98% no cuts in 2026 | Polymarket ($10.8M and $12.3M volume) | Medium (verify against Fed communications) | Hawkish, pressures high-multiple tech |
| AI bubble | 62% "bubble burst in 2026," up 54.7pp in a week | Polymarket ($3.3M volume) | Medium | Sentiment has flipped sharply |

**Bottom line**: the evidence points to a sharp, sector-wide AI selloff overlaid on a hawkish Fed. AMD has company-specific overhangs from the short report and the China export headlines. I can't confirm price levels or macro data, so that call belongs with the next agent weighing the trade.

**Scope and data caveats**

**Derived valuation observations**
- **Price/sales:** about 15.5x TTM.
- **EV/EBITDA:** about 63x, using debt of roughly $9.2B (D/E × equity) and cash of $7.4B. Cash excludes short-term investments, which the tool did not show.
- **Forward P/E vs TTM:** the forward P/E of 24x compares with 91x trailing. Forward EPS of $17.64 is about 3.8x TTM GAAP EPS. It is almost certainly a non-GAAP, forward-year consensus figure, so it is not like-for-like with GAAP EPS. Q3 GAAP EPS of $1.46 annualizes to about $5.84.
- **Price check:** P/E × EPS and forward P/E × forward EPS both imply a share price of about **$424**. This conflicts with:
  - insider sales at **$502–$526 on Nov 16** and **$511 on Nov 17**;
  - a 50-day average of $555.

  Either the stock fell about 17% in the last 3 days, or the snapshot is stale or inconsistent. Verify the live price before using any valuation multiple above.
- **Vendor inconsistencies:**
  - TTM gross profit of $25.44B implies a 56.0% margin. Recent GAAP quarterly margins are 52.8–53.9%, and the implied Q4'25 margin would be an implausible ~64%. This is likely a definitional difference.
  - The vendor operating margin of 17.8% does not match the Q3'26 computed 21.2%.

---

## 2. Income statement (GAAP, quarterly, $M)

| Quarter | Revenue | Gross profit | GM % | Op income | Op margin | Net income | Diluted EPS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q3'25 (Sep-25) | 9,246 | 4,780 | 51.7% | 1,270 | 13.7% | 1,243 | 0.75 |
| Q1'26 (Mar-26) | 10,253 | 5,416 | 52.8% | 1,476 | 14.4% | 1,383 | 0.84 |
| Q2'26 (Jun-26) | 11,536 | 6,203 | 53.8% | 1,990 | 17.3% | 2,297 | 1.38 |
| **Q3'26 (Sep-26)** | **13,377** | **7,210** | **53.9%** | **2,832** | **21.2%** | **2,428** | **1.46** |

**Growth and leverage**
- **Revenue growth:** +44.7% YoY in Q3'26 (vs +50.1% in Q2'26 and +37.8% in Q1'26). Sequential growth was +12.5% in Q2 and +16.0% in Q3.
- **EPS and net income:** both roughly doubled YoY in Q3 (EPS $1.46 vs $0.75, +95%).
- **Operating leverage:** implied opex (gross profit minus operating income) was $4,378M in Q3'26, up 24.7% YoY against revenue up 44.7%. Opex fell from 38.0% to 32.7% of revenue. Incremental operating margin was about 46% in Q3 (+$842M operating income on +$1,841M revenue) and about 40% in Q2.
- **Gross margin:** still expanding slowly, from 51.7% to 53.9% YoY.
- **Q2'25 comparison:** operating income was -$134M and gross margin about 39.8% that quarter, which points to a one-off charge. The year-ago comps are easy.
- **Implied Q4'25:** about $10.27B revenue, $1.6B net income and about $1.00 EPS (TTM minus the three 2026 quarters).
- **Long-term history:**
  - Revenue was $832M in Q1'16, so it is up about 16x to $13.4B.
  - Operating income was negative or near zero through 2017.
